item.title: Two critically injured after car ploughs into crowd of Newcastle Knights supporters
item.description: Emergency services are treating multiple casualties after a car crashed into a crowd during a Newcastle Knights pre-grand final farewell.

media:group.media:description: Emergency services at the scene of a car crash at a Newcastle Knights supporters gathering today.

item.title: Beau Lamarre-Condon was impassive until his former friend testified against him
item.description: For the bulk of his murder trial former police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon has remained impassive, except for when his former friends have been on the stand testifying against him.

media:group.media:description: Beau Lamarre-Condon has pleaded not guilty to two counts of domestic violence-related murder and one of aggravated break and enter.

item.title: 'It breaks you': Friend of stabbed hero pilot speaks out
item.description: A pilot and close friend of the Indian flydubai captain who was attacked during a flight to Israel recalls his shock upon first seeing footage of the incident online.

media:group.media:description: Dhaval Patel celebrates getting his captain's stripe with his wife and Smit Machchhar.

item.title: Magnitude-4.8 earthquake rattles rural Victoria
item.description: Geoscience Australia says the quake hit at a shallow depth of 10 kilometres just after 2am, and that the epicentre was near Leongatha, about 135km south-east of Melbourne.

media:group.media:description: The 4.8-magnitude earthquake was felt near Leongatha, Geoscience Australia reported.

item.title: The world is facing a bigger 'excursion into hell' than it did with Iraq
item.description: What so many of the current major global conflicts have in common with the debacle in Iraq is their undefined, or sometimes not truthfully defined, missions.
item.dc:creator: Laura Tingle

media:group.media:description: Donald Trump observed this week that the US's ventures into Iraq this century have been a "very expensive excursion into hell".

item.title: New York says Cornell 'gang-rape' case now active criminal investigation
item.description: Kathy Hochul says the woman who accused a group of Cornell University students of rape has been "failed" at "every turn" by authorities.
item.dc:creator: Brad Ryan

media:group.media:description: Kathy Hochul (left) says she has lost faith in local authorities and has asked Letitia James to oversee a new investigation.

item.title: Australia's power supply forecasts have never been rosier. Experts are worried
item.description: Historically, forecasting power reliability was a sober task. Experts say Australia is now counting on projects that will never be built.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Mercer

media:group.media:description: Experts fear the way Australia's energy operator assesses future power reliability obscures problems.

item.title: Swiss count cost of 'unprecedented' glacier melting over European summer
item.description: Europe's record-breaking summer has led to "staggering" melting on Switzerland's famous glaciers, according to a new report.
item.dc:creator: Mazoe Ford

media:group.media:description: A drone view from July shows the retreat of the Rhone glacier.

item.title: A 'bent' syringe, a closed curtain: Inside Christa Pike's botched US execution
item.description: Convicted killer Christa Pike remains in hospital receiving emergency treatment after surviving two doses of the lethal injection drug pentobarbital.

media:group.media:description: Christa Pike, seen here in 2007, had been on death row for more than 30 years.

item.title: Complaint over senior NT public servant who ran private NDIS provider
item.description: A senior staffer with the Northern Territory's Department of Children and Families in Central Australia spent almost three years as the sole director of a private NDIS provider in Alice Springs.
item.dc:creator: James Elton

media:group.media:description: Kudzai Mutsunge was the sole director of Life Aspects for almost three years.

item.title: Data centre operator Firmus about to float as its owner tries to shed jailbird image
item.description: He went to prison for insider trading but Oliver Curtis is about to be the source of one of Australia's largest share market floats.
item.dc:creator: Ian Verrender

media:group.media:description: Stockbroker Oliver Curtis and his wife Roxy Jacenko arrive at the NSW Supreme Court, June 17, 2016.

item.title: Brisbane 2032 emblems leaked by official YouTube channel
item.description: The emblems for the Brisbane 2032 Olympics and Paralympics have been accidentally leaked by the Games' official YouTube channel, ruining its own grand unveiling slated for Monday.
item.dc:creator: Henry Hanson

media:group.media:description: The official Brisbane 2032 YouTube channel seemingly ruined the grand unveiling of its own emblem.

item.title: G7 to release 100 million barrels of oil in bid to curb soaring prices
item.description: The announcement from French President Emmanuel Macron came after US President Donald Trump ramped up pressure on Europe to release reserves.

media:group.media:description: The G7 talks were convened by Emmanuel Macron after a conversation with US President Donald Trump.

item.title: Victoria is about to have the most unpredictable election in living memory
item.description: Much has been written about the rise of Pauline Hanson's One Nation in the past 12 months. The Victorian election will give us our best look yet at the decline of the two-party system.

media:group.media:description: Liberal Jess Wilson, Labor's Ben Carroll and One Nation's Warren Pickering all hope to be Victoria's next premier.

item.title: Violent protests in France over conditions in high schools
item.description: French students and police have accused each other of violence as protests continue over conditions in education.

media:group.media:description: French students are protesting for greater resources and improved conditions in schools.

item.title: Man charged with preparing terrorist acts against Nigel Farage
item.description: Joshua Kerry had already been charged with the murder of former British MP Ann Widdecombe and has now been charged with preparing acts of terrorism.

media:group.media:description: British police have charged a man with preparing acts of terrorism, including against Nigel Farage.

item.title: Flydubai 'hero' pilot says praying gave him courage
item.description: Captain Smit Machchhar has been hailed a hero for his actions aboard a flydubai flight after his co-pilot stabbed him and the plane began a steep descent.

media:group.media:description: Smit Machchhar talks with Narendra Modi from hospital.

item.title: Concreter survives three deadly strokes, warns against ignoring symptoms
item.description: A Queensland stroke survivor is overhauling his life and spreading awareness of symptoms after nearly dying this year, as experts say rushing to hospital as soon as possible is critical.
item.dc:creator: Madeline Grace

media:group.media:description: Dru Arnold says it has been an emotional journey for him and his wife Josie.

item.title: Ivory still legal to sell in Australia despite 2019 promise to ban it
item.description: A new study has found hardly any of the $1.2 million worth of elephant ivory sold or advertised in a six-month period in Australia came with paperwork proving its origin.
item.dc:creator: Peter de Kruijff

media:group.media:description: Elephant ivory is being traded domestically in Australia amid international calls to ban the practice.

item.title: Tedesco and Ponga went through different worlds to meet in NRL grand final
item.description: On Sunday, opposing fullbacks James Tedesco and Kalyn Ponga will lead their teams into the NRL grand final. It's about the only thing their paths have had in common.

media:group.media:description: Ponga and Tedesco will lead their NRL teams into the grand final on Sunday.

item.title: Roosters met with Rabbi Eli Schlanger days before Bondi attack
item.description: Five days before one of Australia's darkest days, a group of Sydney Roosters players visited a Bondi synagogue. What happened next would change the meaning of that meeting forever.
item.dc:creator: Myles Houlbrook-Walk and Henry Hanson

media:group.media:description: Rabbi Yehoram Ulman (pictured) and Rabbi Eli Schlanger met with a group of Sydney Roosters players days before the Bondi attacks.

item.title: Soldiers' surprise backyard makeover leaves 90yo 'stunned'
item.description: Pouring into the homes of two war widows, more than 20 soldiers were on a mission to beautify their backyards. Both women were "beyond grateful" for the help, as the Legacy program nears its 10th birthday.
item.dc:creator: Katrina Beavan

media:group.media:description: Vera Walker describes her backyard makeover as "absolutely beautiful".

item.title: Graziers step in to fix damaged roads after incomes 'decimated'
item.description: Transport for NSW will hire graziers to fix roads damaged by months of heavy rain in the remote Far West. But some graziers say red tape is slowing down progress and repairs.

media:group.media:description: Sam Maiden of Mt Gipps Station says the new initiative is "not fit for purpose".

item.title: One Nation makes election promise to revive Victoria's timber sector
item.description: One Nation has promised to resume native timber logging in Victoria if it wins the state election, but the party would not say if it has costed the policy.
item.dc:creator: Madeleine Stuchbery and Jarrod Whittaker

media:group.media:description: One Nation has pledged to let loggers back into native forests in Victoria if it wins the state election.

item.title: Labor's working holiday visa policy risks regional seats, experts say
item.description: Political experts say the immigration policy changes put Labor's regional MPs in a tight spot to represent their community and defend their party.
item.dc:creator: Rosanne Maloney and Conor Byrne

media:group.media:description: Italian backpacker Rocco Raseri's visa for a third year is no longer guaranteed.
